title: Reduce heap pressure in observability stack; mmap-backed log writer + OTel compatibility shim
creator: Avery Marshall
description:
Background: Our runtime's observability hot-path (request tracing + logging + local metric aggregation) is a significant source of allocation churn and occasional GC spikes on p95/p99 workloads. Recent customer incidents surfaced that under sustained 100qps traffic with long sequences we see 20-40% CPU increase and visible tail latency due to GC pauses caused by per-request log buffer allocations and high-cardinality transient label maps.

Goal: Reduce steady-state allocations and tail GC pressure from the observability stack without changing user-facing traces/metrics semantics. Target goals: reduce allocations per request in the hot path by >= 30%, lower CPU used by observability by >= 10%, and bring p99 latency overhead from observability to < 3ms for the typical generation request profile.

Proposed changes (high level):
1) mmap-backed append-only log writer: build a lightweight writer that uses a pre-allocated mmap region per process (with rotation) to serialize structured log lines and small trace events with zero-copy buffers into the region, and flush pages asynchronously to disk or to an onward shipper. This removes the need for per-request allocation of log buffers in the hot path.

2) pooled, reusable envelope buffers: replace current per-request map->json allocations by using a small pool of reusable byte slices and a zero-allocation JSON encoder path for our constrained schema (timestamp + level + trace_id + message + compact tags).

3) OTel compatibility shim (OTLP minimal): implement a thin compatibility layer that translates our internal trace/span objects into an OTLP-compliant protobuf stream on a hot path that minimizes allocations (pre-allocated proto messages, re-usable ID encoders). The goal is parity with exported fields but with a deterministic allocation budget.

4) Hot-path sync -> lock-free ring buffer for metric events: where feasible, replace mutex-protected buffers with an atomic ring buffer that drains in a background goroutine (or equivalent for runtime language), to reduce contention and heap churn under bursty traffic.

5) Cardinatlity hygiene: enforce an explicit whitelist of metric label keys in the hot path and move rare labels to a slower path to avoid building high-cardinality maps per request.

Rollout plan:
- Spike/prototype (week 1): mmap writer PoC and bench against current writer. Microbench results expected in < 3 days.
- Implementation (week 2): integrate pooled buffers + ring buffer, add OTel shim.
- Integration test and perf harness (week 3): run canary harness simulating long-sequence, 100qps workload with synthetic traces; validate nothing is lost and metrics match existing baselines.
- Canary (week 4): enable for 10% of runtime traffic with observability feature flag; monitor error rates, memory, GC, latency.
- Full rollout (week 5-6): gradual ramp if canary stable.

Trade-offs & risks:
- mmap introduces complexity around rotation and persistence semantics; must ensure we don't lose events on crash if pages not flushed. We'll set expectations (best-effort local persistence) and rely on onward shipping for durable storage.
- OTel shim complexity: must keep parity with downstream dashboards; will plan a short verification suite to compare spans/attributes pre/post.
- Some languages/runtimes on our platform may not support mmap the same way; this ticket will implement in the Go runtime first and provide an abstracted interface for other runtimes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmarks show >= 30% reduction in allocations per request in the observability hot path.
- Observability-related CPU drops by >= 10% on the perf harness.
- No increase in dropped telemetry events; exports parity tests pass.
- Canary run for 48 hours at 10% with no visible error-rate regression or increased latency beyond 2x current (target absolute p99 overhead < 3ms).
- Code review + security review sign-off for mmap and buffer management.

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on runtime-level allocation and hot-path optimizations. Larger architectural reworks (moving to a sidecar collector or full OTEL SDK replacement) are out of scope for this task and will be captured as follow-ups.

2026-03-04 - Ravi: Implemented pooled buffers and integrated zero-alloc JSON encoder. Bench microresults: allocations/request down ~28% overall; still missing the 30% target for combined traces+logs.
2026-03-05 - QA: Integration test found intermittent drop of low-volume trace attributes during ring buffer overflow in corner case; added backpressure guards and metric for overflow_count.
2026-03-07 - Security: flagged potential mmap permission hardening; requested a short threat model for local mmap files and owner-only perms. Ravi: will apply 0600 and transient tmpfs by default.
2026-03-09 - Perf: End-to-end harness shows observability CPU down 12% at 100qps; p99 overhead reduced to 2.6ms. Need to run 48h canary.
2026-03-11 - Code Review: PR feedback to add stronger null-safety in the OTel shim and add unit tests for proto reuse; addressed in follow-up commit.
2026-03-12 - Ravi: Started canary rollout (10%); initial observability dashboard shows steady memory and stable error rates.)
